The games

Eleven tiny games. All good fun.

0167 Calculator

All roads lead to 67. Unless the math actually does.

A fully working calculator with exactly one answer. Go on, try some sums on this one.

Open the calculator

02Excuse Generator

A perfectly good excuse. Believability sold separately.

Pick your situation and the Department of Plausible Explanations handles the rest.

Get an excuse

03Rock Paper Scissors

Three choices. One finger gun. Skill issue.

The classic, more or less. Pick your move and trust your instincts. Probably.

Make my move

04Wordle for Dummies

Five letters. Six chances. Surely you’ve got this.

The real rules and a real list of 14,855 words. It should be easy. It is not.

Play Wordle for Dummies

05Fortune Cookie

A little wisdom. A little disrespect.

Crack one open and see what fate has to say. Fate has opinions.

06IQ Test

Ten questions. One very confident assessment.

Rigorous questions, carefully chosen answers, and a score you will remember.

07Horoscope

Written in the stars. Probably a typo.

08The Sorting Hat

Five questions. Four houses. One very opinionated hat.

An unofficial sorting ceremony run by a hat with absolutely no qualifications.

Sort me

09To-Do Tabloid

10Dog Time Converter

Your five-minute errand was a whole saga to the dog.

About

Tiny games.
Big chuckles.

The Dumb Little Internet is a growing collection of tiny browser games and silly tools.

Spin the wheel or press a key, pick a game, and you are playing in seconds. There is nothing to download, no account to make and no instructions to read.

It was designed for one reason: a good chuckle.

Every game takes about a minute. None of them will make you more productive, and all of them are happy not to be taken seriously.
